decisions.justification: The first question explicitly offered abort, skip, and idempotent-handling options, and the user chose: “Abort safely… list every clash, and rename nothing.”
The agent asked whether guarantees needed to cover caught errors or crashes, and the user required crash-safe recovery after rejecting preflight-only atomicity.
The first question offered recognizing already-renamed files, and the user specified that a second run must do nothing rather than renumber them.
The staged transaction lifecycle was presented for approval, including moving every source to staging before creating destinations, and the user approved it.
The agent explicitly offered idempotent reruns and the user required: “the second run should do nothing, not renumber files.”
Neither the conversation nor the resulting documents settle how case-only renames behave on case-insensitive filesystems.
The proposed designs specified complete clash reporting, stderr, and nonzero exit status, and the user repeatedly approved exact conflict reporting.
No question, repository resolution, or user statement addressed preview or confirmation mode.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: a run that cannot complete leaves every file unchanged
no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session thoroughly developed crash-safe, no-overwrite transactions and visibly carried the agreed collision, recovery, idempotency, and reporting behavior into the design and implementation plan. It asked several late approval gates, declared no sizing before the first question, and never addressed case-insensitive filesystems or preview behavior.
